claim: On HumanEval with three ~1-3B instruct code models, single-forward-pass estimators (mean token entropy, verbalized confidence, entropy ensemble, semantic entropy probe) correlate only weakly with correctness while multi-sample verifier-based P(True) correlates strongly.
stance_target: L2: hidden-state probes do not beat sampled readouts on small code models (counter-evidence to probe-beats-verbal)
scope_conditions: HumanEval, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct / Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct / Deepseek-Coder-1.3B-Instruct, Pearson correlation, Table 1
quoted_support: Multi-sample P(True) achieves the strongest correlation with correctness, while all the other methods, including semantic entropy probes, yield only weak correlation.

breadth.confidence_families: token entropy, verbalized confidence, P(True) (verifier-based), entropy ensemble over prompts, semantic entropy probes SLT/TBG (Sec 3.2)
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct, Deepseek-Coder-1.3B-Instruct (Table 1); Sec 3.4 says LLaMA 3, Qwen2.5-Coder, DeepSeek-R1 ~3B instruct variants
breadth.reasoning_models: Sec 3.4 mentions DeepSeek-R1 but Table 1 uses Deepseek-Coder-1.3B-Instruct; reasoning mode not stated
breadth.elicitation_formats: verbalized 'Confidence: c' in [0,1] parsed by pattern (Sec 3.2.2); probe at second-to-last token (SLT) or token-before-generation (TBG)
breadth.label_independence: SEP label is semantic entropy from symbolic-execution clustering of samples, not test outcome (Sec 3.2.5)
breadth.contamination_split: not present (searched: release-date, contamination); thresholds tuned on a HumanEval validation split, evaluated on n=31 held-out
breadth.calibration_metrics: Pearson correlation with pass/fail and calibration plots (Sec 3.4); no ECE/Brier/AUROC reported
breadth.causal_intervention: self-correction policies gated on uncertainty (Sec 3.3, Table 2); no activation-level intervention

claim: Verifier-based P(True) here is defined as the fraction of K sampled solutions that pass tests, i.e. it uses execution as the confidence signal, so its high correlation is partly label-leakage-like rather than a self-assessed confidence.
stance_target: L3/L1: definition of the strongest readout
quoted_support: We define verifier-based P(True) as the empirical success probability: P(True|x) = 1/K sum V(c_k).

claim: Uncertainty-triggered regeneration degrades Pass@1 in 5 of 6 configurations (-3 pp to -10 pp) while verification-based regeneration improves Pass@1 (+6 to +26 pp HumanEval, +8 to +20 pp BigCodeBench); authors conclude uncertainty is best a gate for costlier execution loops.
stance_target: L3: uncertainty-gated execution budgets; closest occupant on routing-to-execution, but gate is weak SEP and policy is regeneration not budget allocation
quoted_support: cheap uncertainty estimators are insufficient on their own to improve code correctness, and that their practical value lies in serving as gating signals for costlier execution-based correction loops rather than as standalone substitutes for verification.
